themes_detail.label: Dead animals spike
themes_detail.summary: Park Slope residents filed 11 dead animal complaints last week—a 780% spike from the 1.2-per-week average—signaling a potential public health concern that warrants immediate investigation into whether this reflects seasonal wildlife die-off, disease, or neglected disposal.
evidence: 11 dead animal complaints last week vs. 1.2-per-week baseline (z-score: 10.07)
780% increase from 8-week average—highest statistical anomaly in dataset
Coincides with seasonal wildlife activity patterns (spring)
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Parks and Sanitation Department about response protocols and whether complaints reflect actual spike or delayed reporting
Canvass Park Slope residents and local veterinarians about potential wildlife disease outbreak or unusual animal mortality

themes_detail.label: Street noise surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 33 this week—181% above the 11.8-per-week average—representing the most acute quality-of-life disruption emerging in the district and suggesting either new construction activity, event traffic, or nightlife disturbances.
evidence: 33 noise complaints this week vs. 11.8-per-week baseline (z-score: 6.5)
Aligns with 1,185 active DOB building permits (157 new buildings) that may be driving daytime/nighttime disruption
reporting_angles: Map complaint clusters to identify whether noise is concentrated near active construction zones (46 Nelson Street, GSD projects, Gowanus facilities)
Interview residents near highest-complaint blocks and DOB contractors about noise mitigation compliance

themes_detail.label: Tree hazards accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints spiked 433% last week (8 vs. 1.5 weekly average) and dead/dying tree complaints jumped 700% two weeks ago (3 vs. 0.4 average), indicating neglected Parks maintenance that creates sidewalk and property safety risks.
evidence: 8 overgrown tree complaints last week vs. 1.5-per-week baseline (433% increase, z-score: 5.31)
3 dead/dying tree complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 average (700% increase, z-score: 3.77)
Long-standing community board request for 'reconstruct or upgrade a building in a park' suggests chronic under-maintenance
reporting_angles: Analyze NYC Parks budget and staffing data for CD306 to assess whether arborist crew capacity is inadequate
Document specific tree hazards (low-hanging branches, dead limbs) in parks and on streets; photograph before/after removal

themes_detail.label: Homeless assistance surge
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance requests jumped to 19 three weeks ago—485% above the 3.2-per-week baseline—reflecting either increased visibility of unhoused populations or inadequate shelter capacity driving street-level crisis.
evidence: 19 homeless assistance complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 3.2-per-week baseline (485% increase, z-score: 4.61)
Consistent community board budget request for 'Other request for services for the homeless' suggests ongoing unmet need
$24M Gowanus composting facility completed (April 2026) but no parallel investment in shelter/services mentioned
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Department of Homeless Services about whether CD306 shelter bed capacity is sufficient; map shelter locations
Canvass street workers and parks staff about where unhoused populations are clustering and what services are being requested

themes_detail.label: Street deterioration pattern
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints peaked at 121 three weeks ago—354% above the 26.6-per-week average (z-score: 4.99)—suggesting infrastructure degradation that may relate to winter weather damage or deferred maintenance now surfacing.
evidence: 121 street condition complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 26.6-per-week baseline (354% increase, z-score: 4.99)
Snow/ice complaints remain high (1,141 over 90 days), suggesting winter damage not yet repaired
Community board repeatedly requests 'Inspect water main on specific street segment and repair or replace' (DEP agenda item)
reporting_angles: Request NYC DOT street inspection maps and repair schedules to identify which avenues/blocks in CD306 are prioritized
Document specific hazardous street sections (potholes, buckled pavement) with photos and resident impact stories
